userStories.title: Fleet write descriptors and jobPath
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the three fleet write tool descriptors (`KODA_DISPATCH_JOB`, `KODA_REQUEUE_JOB`, `KODA_CANCEL_JOB`) and `FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` appended last in `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`, and move `jobPath` from `tools/fleet-tools.ts` to an export of `tools/tool-input.ts`.

**Motivation** — Today a thread can read jobs but cannot start, retry or stop one; the agent only sees a tool once its descriptor is in the list sent to the runner.

**Approach** — 2b2-D1 Descriptors: `FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` is `[KODA_DISPATCH_JOB, KODA_REQUEUE_JOB, KODA_CANCEL_JOB]`, appended after `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` in `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`. REPO and PROJECT threads get 22 descriptors, WORKSPACE 23 (`KODA_TOOL_LIMITS.maxTools` is 32). Each description says the job is started, requeued or cancelled "only after the user approves" and tells the agent "do not call this tool again" for the same request, matching the 2b-1 wording. Every description stays at most 2000 characters once the WORKSPACE sentence is appended (the runner rejects the whole list otherwise, `apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts`).

2b2-D3 Input bounds (the inputSchema mirrors them; the tool's `parse` enforces them in US-003..005):
- dispatch `repo`: required; string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` (owner/name)
- dispatch `command`: required; `RUN` or `PLAN`
- dispatch `feature`: required; string of 1 to 128 characters
- dispatch `maxCostUsd`: required; finite number, at least 0.0001, at most 10000, at most 4 decimal places (the dispatch DTO's bounds)
- dispatch `ref`: optional; string of 1 to 255 characters
- dispatch `planFrom`: optional; string of 1 to 512 characters
- dispatch `profiles`: optional; array of at most 8 strings, each 1 to 64 characters
- dispatch `bashMode`: optional; `raw`, `gated` or `escalate`
- dispatch `ticketRefs`: optional; array of 1 to 20 strings each matching `TICKET_REF`
- requeue, cancel `jobId`: required; string of 1 to 64 characters

2b2-D2 Permissions (registered later by `FleetWriteTools`): `koda_dispatch_job`: `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'create', subject: 'FleetJob' }`; `koda_requeue_job` and `koda_cancel_job`: `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'update', subject: 'FleetJob' }`.

2b2-D8: `jobPath` moves from a private helper of `tools/fleet-tools.ts` to an export of `tools/tool-input.ts`, unchanged; `fleet-tools.ts` imports it. `asRecord` and `ticketPath` unchanged.

Existing spec updates in `koda-tool-descriptors.spec.ts`: the test `gives REPO and PROJECT 19 descriptors and WORKSPACE 20` becomes 22 and 23 and its `at(-1)` name check becomes `koda_cancel_job`; the 2b-1 tests `AC-4: REPO answers 19 descriptors` and `AC-5: WORKSPACE answers 20 descriptors` become 22 and 23; the 2b-1 test `AC-2: REPO ends with the WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entries` asserts instead that the five write entries directly precede the three `FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` entries; every slice that offsets by `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length` (the `AC-3` and `AC-15` tests naming `koda_get_action` and `koda_add_comment`, and the `AC-22` prefix tests that also subtract `ACTION_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length`) offsets by `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length + FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length` instead; the `AC-22` full-list equality of `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` gains `...FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` last. No other assertion changes. `tool-input.spec.ts` gains a `jobPath` test; the existing two tests are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: the three descriptors and the group constant, `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` append, `jobPath` move, spec updates above. Out: the tools' parse/preview/execute, the `FleetWriteTools` provider, `fleetWriteRefusal` (US-002..US-005). Every existing descriptor stays unchanged.

**Interface**
```typescript
// koda-tool-descriptors.ts
export const KODA_DISPATCH_JOB: KodaToolDescriptor
export const KODA_REQUEUE_JOB: KodaToolDescriptor
export const KODA_CANCEL_JOB: KodaToolDescriptor
export const FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS: readonly KodaToolDescriptor[] // [KODA_DISPATCH_JOB, KODA_REQUEUE_JOB, KODA_CANCEL_JOB]
// KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS = [...TICKET, ...FLEET, ...KNOWLEDGE, ...ACTION, ...WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS, ...FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS]

// tools/tool-input.ts
export function jobPath(slug: string, jobId: string): string // `/${slug}/fleet/jobs/${jobId}`
```
acceptanceCriteria: FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.map((d) => d.name) equals ['koda_dispatch_job', 'koda_requeue_job', 'koda_cancel_job']
The last three entries of kodaToolDescriptorsFor('REPO') are the FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entries, in order
The five entries of kodaToolDescriptorsFor('REPO') before those three are the WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entries, in order
kodaToolDescriptorsFor('REPO') has 22 entries
kodaToolDescriptorsFor('WORKSPACE') has 23 entries
Every FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entry's description contains 'only after the user approves'
Every FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entry's description contains 'do not call this tool again'
KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.required equals ['repo', 'command', 'feature', 'maxCostUsd']
KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.properties.command.enum equals ['RUN', 'PLAN']
KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.properties.maxCostUsd.minimum equals 0.0001
KODA_DISPATCH_JOB.inputSchema.properties.maxCostUsd.maximum equals 10000
KODA_REQUEUE_JOB.inputSchema.required equals ['jobId']
KODA_CANCEL_JOB.inputSchema.required equals ['jobId']
jobPath('web', 'j1'), imported from tools/tool-input.ts, returns '/web/fleet/jobs/j1'

routing.reasoning: Additive descriptors plus a function move, but several existing descriptor-spec assertions must be updated precisely; convention-sensitive and standard patterns, no new abstractions.

suggestedCriteria: Every FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entry's description is at most 2000 characters once the WORKSPACE sentence is appended
The fleet read tools in tools/fleet-tools.ts return the same job path links as before after jobPath is imported from tools/tool-input.ts

modifiedFiles.reason: gains `KODA_DISPATCH_JOB`, `KODA_REQUEUE_JOB`, `KODA_CANCEL_JOB` and `FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`, appended last in `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` (2b2-D1); every existing descriptor unchanged.

the three fleet write descriptors are appended after the write group, so: the test `gives REPO and PROJECT 19 descriptors and WORKSPACE 20` becomes 22 and 23 and its `at(-1)` name check becomes `koda_cancel_job`; the 2b-1 tests `AC-4: REPO answers 19 descriptors` and `AC-5: WORKSPACE answers 20 descriptors` become 22 and 23; the 2b-1 test `AC-2: REPO ends with the WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS entries` asserts instead that the five write entries directly precede the three `FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` entries; every slice that offsets by `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length` (the `AC-3` and `AC-15` tests naming `koda_get_action` and `koda_add_comment`, and the `AC-22` prefix tests that also subtract `ACTION_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length`) offsets by `WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length + FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length` instead; the `AC-22` full-list equality of `KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` gains `...FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` last. No other assertion changes.
imports `jobPath` from the shared tool-input helper module instead of declaring it (2b2-D8); behaviour unchanged.
gains the exported `jobPath(slug, jobId)` helper moved from the fleet read tools module; `asRecord` and `ticketPath` unchanged.
gains a `jobPath` test; the existing two tests unchanged.

userStories.title: Fleet refusal text
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `fleetWriteRefusal(error: unknown): string | null` in `tools/fleet-write-refusal.ts`, turning the fleet services' 409 and 400 refusals into a one-line reason.

**Motivation** — Today any `AppException` other than not-found that an `execute` throws becomes `error: <tool> failed`, which hides why a dispatch did not happen.

**Approach** — 2b2-D7 Refusal text: `fleetWriteRefusal(error: unknown): string | null` reads an `AppException`'s `prefix` and `args`:

| Exception | `prefix` | Text |
|---|---|---|
| `ConflictAppException` | `fleet.jobState` | `job is <args.state>` |
| `ConflictAppException` | `fleet.jobs` | `job <args.activeJobId> is already active for this feature` |
| `ConflictAppException` | `fleet.dispatchOpenPr` | `open PR on <args.refs>` |
| `BudgetPausedException` | `fleet.budgetPaused` | `budget paused for <args.scope>` |
| `ConflictAppException` | `fleet.configRequeue` | `the config edit ended <args.outcome>` |
| `ValidationAppException` | `fleet.dispatchInput` | `invalid <args.reason>` |
| anything else | — | null |

Read the real exception shapes from `common/exceptions/conflict-app.exception.ts`, `fleet/budgets/budget.exceptions.ts`, and the throw sites in `fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts` and `fleet/jobs/dispatch-input.ts` (`fail`) before coding; `BudgetPausedException` carries the policy's `scopeKey` in `args.scope`. `AppException.prefix` / `.args` come from `@nathapp/nestjs-common`.

**Scope** — In: the helper and its unit spec. Out: any tool, descriptor or provider (US-001, US-003..US-005). The helper does not wrap or throw; it only returns text or null.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function fleetWriteRefusal(error: unknown): string | null
```
acceptanceCriteria: fleetWriteRefusal(new ConflictAppException({ state: 'RUNNING' }, 'fleet.jobState')) returns 'job is RUNNING'
fleetWriteRefusal(new ConflictAppException({ activeJobId: 'j9' }, 'fleet.jobs')) returns 'job j9 is already active for this feature'
fleetWriteRefusal(new ConflictAppException({ refs: 'WEB-1, WEB-2' }, 'fleet.dispatchOpenPr')) returns 'open PR on WEB-1, WEB-2'
fleetWriteRefusal for a BudgetPausedException built from a policy whose scopeKey is 'project:p1' returns 'budget paused for project:p1'
fleetWriteRefusal(new ConflictAppException({ outcome: 'conflict' }, 'fleet.configRequeue')) returns 'the config edit ended conflict'
fleetWriteRefusal(new ValidationAppException({ reason: 'ticket WEB-9' }, 'fleet.dispatchInput')) returns 'invalid ticket WEB-9'
fleetWriteRefusal(new ConflictAppException({}, 'threads.busy')) returns null
fleetWriteRefusal(new Error('boom')) returns null

routing.reasoning: Single pure function mapping exception prefix/args to text; new file plus its spec, no integration.

userStories.title: koda_dispatch_job
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `dispatchJobTool` and the `FleetWriteTools` provider, registered in `AssistantModule`, so a thread can propose a RUN or PLAN dispatch that runs `FleetJobsService.dispatch` as the requester on approval.

**Motivation** — S5b-R4 puts fleet dispatch in scope for the assistant ("plan this spec"); today the user must leave the thread for the fleet page.

**Approach** — Rulings: 2b2-R1 `koda_dispatch_job` calls `FleetJobsService.dispatch` directly and does **not** bind the job to the thread: no `threadId` option (the thread hand-off path locks an idle thread and the calling thread is never idle while its turn runs, so it would always answer `threads.busy`). 2b2-R2 `maxCostUsd` is required, no default cost. 2b2-R3 A RUN whose tickets already have an open VCS PR fails the action; no `acknowledgeOpenPr` input. 2b2-R6 `koda_dispatch_job` takes no `pinnedRunnerId`, `selectorLabels`, `approvalTimeoutSec` or `acknowledgeOpenPr`; they keep the defaults `normalizeDispatch` applies.

2b2-D3 Input bounds, checked by `parse`; a violation throws `ToolInputError(<field>)`:
- `repo`: required; string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`
- `command`: required; `RUN` or `PLAN`
- `feature`: required; string of 1 to 128 characters (`normalizeDispatch` applies the nax feature-name rule at preview)
- `maxCostUsd`: required; a finite number, at least 0.0001, at most 10000, at most 4 decimal places, judged as `Number(x.toFixed(4)) === x`
- `ref`: optional; string of 1 to 255 characters
- `planFrom`: optional; string of 1 to 512 characters
- `profiles`: optional; array of at most 8 strings, each 1 to 64 characters
- `bashMode`: optional; `raw`, `gated` or `escalate`
- `ticketRefs`: optional; array of 1 to 20 strings each matching `TICKET_REF`

2b2-D4 Preview format. Every preview is masked with `maskSecrets`. Optional lines appear only when the input has the field, in this order:
```text
Dispatch RUN in web:
repo: acme/app @ trunk
feature: add-auth
max cost: $0.5
plan from: docs/specs/add-auth.md
profiles: native-ds, fast
bash: escalate
tickets: WEB-1, WEB-2
```
The ref is the input `ref`, or the repository's default branch when absent. The cost is `String(maxCostUsd)`.

2b2-D5 Preview checks (the preview is where a proposal is refused, so no action exists for a request that cannot run): the repository resolves through `KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo(ctx.projectId, { owner, name })`, else `NotFoundAppException` (the executor answers `not_found`). Then `normalizeDispatch(dto, repo.defaultBranch)` runs; its `ValidationAppException` becomes `ToolInputError(<its args.reason>)`.

2b2-D6 Execution runs as the requester: `FleetJobsService.dispatch(ctx.actor.id, ctx.projectId, dto, { ticketActor: { principal: ctx.actor, projectSlug: ctx.projectSlug } })`, with no `threadId` (2b2-R1). `dto` holds the resolved `repoId` and the input's other fields, absent fields left out. `execute` resolves the repository again; when it no longer resolves it throws `NotFoundAppException` before calling the service, so the action is `FAILED` with result `not_found`. Result: `dispatched <jobId>: <state> /<slug>/fleet/jobs/<jobId>` (use `jobPath` from `tools/tool-input.ts`; job id and state come from `DispatchResultDto.job`). A refusal the service throws becomes `ToolActionError('dispatch refused: <text>')` where `<text>` is `fleetWriteRefusal(error)`. When that answers null the error is rethrown, so `NotFoundAppException` still answers `not_found` and anything else `error: <tool> failed`.

2b2-D2 Permission: `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'create', subject: 'FleetJob' }`.

2b2-D8 Files: one file per tool. A new provider `FleetWriteTools` (`tools/fleet-write-tools.ts`) registers the tools in `onModuleInit` as `kind: 'write'` under the US-001 descriptor name, injecting `AssistantToolRegistry`, `FleetJobsService` and `KnowledgeIndexService` (both modules already imported by `AssistantModule`; only the providers list gains `FleetWriteTools`). US-004 and US-005 later register their tools in this file. Mirror `update-ticket-tool.ts` and `ticket-write-tools.ts`.

Integration tests enter at `POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_dispatch_job?leaseEpoch=<n>` and decide at `POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide` (`approvalId` is the stored `PendingAction`'s). Fixtures follow `test/integration/fleet/assistant-update-ticket-tool.integration.spec.ts`: `seedFleetHttpWorld` (project `web` with GitHub repo `acme/app`, default branch `trunk`; foreign project `ops` with `acme/ops`), DEVELOPER `dev`, a RUNNING REPO THREAD job from `seedThreadJobFor` created by `dev`, `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true` before boot. Each propose-then-approve pair is one `it`. Use a feature no other test uses; tests pass in any order (`.nax/rules/api-test-isolation.md`). Needs the compose test DB (`bun run test:db:up`).

**Scope** — In: `dispatch-job-tool.ts`, `fleet-write-tools.ts` (registering only dispatch), `assistant.module.ts` providers, the module registration test, unit and integration specs. Out: `koda_requeue_job` and `koda_cancel_job` (US-004, US-005); descriptors and `jobPath` (US-001); `fleetWriteRefusal` itself (US-002). Also out: binding to the thread (2b2-R1), `acknowledgeOpenPr`, `pinnedRunnerId`, `selectorLabels`, `approvalTimeoutSec`, preview-time `ticketRefs` validation.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function dispatchJobTool(
  fleetJobs: FleetJobsService,
  knowledge: KnowledgeIndexService,
): AssistantTool // parse -> { repo, command, feature, maxCostUsd, ref?, planFrom?, profiles?, bashMode?, ticketRefs? }

@Injectable()
export class FleetWriteTools implements OnModuleInit {
  constructor(registry: AssistantToolRegistry, fleetJobs: FleetJobsService, knowledge: KnowledgeIndexService)
  onModuleInit(): void // registers dispatchJobTool as a write tool
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: dispatchJobTool(...).parse({ repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth' }) throws ToolInputError with reason 'maxCostUsd'

dispatchJobTool(...).preview in project 'web' for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'PLAN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5, planFrom: 'docs/ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789.md' }, when resolveProjectRepo answers acme/app with default branch 'trunk', returns exactly 'Dispatch PLAN in web:
repo: acme/app @ trunk
feature: add-auth
max cost: $0.5
plan from: docs/[masked].md'
dispatchJobTool(...).parse with repo 'app' and otherwise valid input throws ToolInputError with reason 'repo'

dispatchJobTool(...).preview in project 'web' for { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5, ref: 'release', profiles: ['native-ds', 'fast'], bashMode: 'escalate', ticketRefs: ['WEB-1', 'WEB-2'] }, when resolveProjectRepo answers acme/app with default branch 'trunk', returns exactly 'Dispatch RUN in web:
repo: acme/app @ release
feature: add-auth
max cost: $0.5
profiles: native-ds, fast
bash: escalate
tickets: WEB-1, WEB-2'
dispatchJobTool(...).preview for repo 'acme/ops', when KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo answers null, throws NotFoundAppException
dispatchJobTool(...).preview for a PLAN with no planFrom throws ToolInputError with reason 'planFrom required for PLAN'

For dispatchJobTool(...).execute with { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5, ref: 'release', profiles: ['native-ds'], bashMode: 'escalate', ticketRefs: ['WEB-1'] }, when resolveProjectRepo answers repository id 'r1', the third argument FleetJobsService.dispatch receives equals { repoId: 'r1', command: 'RUN', feature: 'add-auth', maxCostUsd: 0.5, ref: 'release', profiles: ['native-ds'], bashMode: 'escalate', ticketRefs: ['WEB-1'] }, with no other key
For dispatchJobTool(...).execute in project 'web', the first two arguments FleetJobsService.dispatch receives are ctx.actor.id and ctx.projectId

For dispatchJobTool(...).execute in project 'web', the fourth argument FleetJobsService.dispatch receives deep-equals { ticketActor: { principal: ctx.actor, projectSlug: 'web' } }, with no threadId key
dispatchJobTool(...).execute in project 'web', when FleetJobsService.dispatch answers a DispatchResultDto whose job has id 'j1' and state 'QUEUED', returns 'dispatched j1: QUEUED /web/fleet/jobs/j1'

dispatchJobTool(...).execute, when FleetJobsService.dispatch throws new ConflictAppException({ refs: 'WEB-1' }, 'fleet.dispatchOpenPr'), throws a ToolActionError whose text is 'dispatch refused: open PR on WEB-1'

In assistant.module.spec.ts, after the compiled AssistantModule testing module runs init(), AssistantToolRegistry.get('koda_dispatch_job')?.permission equals { kind: 'ability', action: 'create', subject: 'FleetJob' }

[integration] POST /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_dispatch_job?leaseEpoch=<n> from the runner holding dev's RUNNING REPO THREAD job, with { repo: 'acme/app', command: 'RUN', feature: <a feature no other test uses>, maxCostUsd: 0.5 }, answers 200 with content starting 'pending '

[integration] After dev approves that action at POST /projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide with { decision: 'approve' }, the project's FleetJob with that feature has requestedById equal to dev's id

[integration] POST /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_dispatch_job?leaseEpoch=<n> from the same runner with repo 'acme/ops' (the foreign project's repository) answers content 'not_found', and no PendingAction exists for that tool call

routing.reasoning: Four new files and a one-line module edit, all following the existing update-ticket-tool and TicketWriteTools pattern with no new abstractions, so single-session TDD suffices despite the integration tests.

suggestedCriteria: dispatchJobTool(...).parse throws ToolInputError with reason 'command' when command is 'CONFIG_EDIT'
dispatchJobTool(...).execute throws NotFoundAppException without calling FleetJobsService.dispatch when resolveProjectRepo answers null
dispatchJobTool(...).execute rethrows the original error when FleetJobsService.dispatch throws an exception for which fleetWriteRefusal answers null
outOfScope: US-003 only: a requester without `create` `FleetJob` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a); this feature adds no AC for it.
US-003 only: an unknown `command` answers `invalid_input: command` from the parser; this feature adds no AC for it.
US-003 only: a `maxCostUsd` below 0.0001, above 10000 or with more than 4 decimal places answers `invalid_input: maxCostUsd` from the parser (2b2-D3); this feature adds no AC for those bounds.
US-003 only: a repository that stops resolving between proposal and approval fails the action with `not_found` (2b2-D6); this feature adds no AC for it.

modifiedFiles.reason: the providers list gains `FleetWriteTools`; no import changes (`FleetJobsModule` and `KnowledgeModule` are already imported).
gains a test that `koda_dispatch_job` is registered as a write tool with its permission; existing tests unchanged.

userStories.title: koda_requeue_job
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `requeueJobTool` and register it in `FleetWriteTools`, so a thread can propose requeueing one CRASHED, FAILED or CANCELLED job of the project, run as the requester on approval.

**Motivation** — The umbrella's example asks include "re-run the job that crashed"; today the user must leave the thread for the fleet page.

**Approach** — 2b2-R4 `koda_requeue_job` needs the CASL ability `update` `FleetJob` (permission `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'update', subject: 'FleetJob' }`). 2b2-R5 A THREAD job is never requeued through a tool; a thread session ends through end-session, as the requeue route already enforces (`fleet-jobs.service.ts`, `requeue`).

2b2-D3 Input: `jobId` required; string of 1 to 64 characters; a violation throws `ToolInputError('jobId')`.

2b2-D4 Preview format (masked with `maskSecrets`):
```text
Requeue job j1 in web:
RUN add-auth on acme/app @ trunk, now FAILED
max cost: $0.5
```
The job line names the repository as `owner/name` through `KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo(projectId, { repoId })`, or as the job's `repoId` when that answers null. The max-cost line shows the job's stored `maxCostUsd` string as it is. The line shows the job's command, feature and ref and its current state.

2b2-D5 Preview checks: the job is read through `FleetJobsService.get(ctx.projectId, jobId)`, so a job of another project answers `not_found`. A THREAD job throws `ToolInputError('command')` (use `isThreadKind` from `fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts`); this check runs before the state check, so a THREAD job in any state answers `command`. Requeue refuses a state `canTransition(state, 'QUEUED', 'server')` (from `fleet/jobs/job-state.ts`) rejects, with `ToolInputError('state')`. CONFIG_EDIT and CONFIG_DRIFT jobs are not restricted; the preview names their command.

2b2-D6 Execution: `FleetJobsService.requeue(ctx.actor.id, ctx.projectId, jobId)`. Result: `requeued <jobId>: <state> /<slug>/fleet/jobs/<jobId>` using the job id and state from the service's `DispatchResultDto.job` and `jobPath`. A refusal the service throws becomes `ToolActionError('requeue refused: <text>')` where `<text>` is `fleetWriteRefusal(error)` (US-002). When that answers null the error is rethrown.

Integration tests (`POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_requeue_job?leaseEpoch=<n>`, decide at `POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide`) follow the fixtures of `assistant-dispatch-job-tool.integration.spec.ts` (created by US-003). The test creates the RUN job it acts on itself, in the state it needs, with `prisma.fleetJob.create` on `acme/app`, the way `seedThreadJobFor` creates the THREAD job, with a feature no other test uses. A job the test approves is created with `selectorLabels: ['no-such-label']`: the requeue keeps the labels, placement reports a `labels` misfit against the fixture runner, and the job stays `QUEUED` instead of taking the runner's one slot. Each propose-then-approve pair is one `it`; tests pass in any order (`.nax/rules/api-test-isolation.md`).

**Scope** — In: `requeue-job-tool.ts`, registering it in `FleetWriteTools.onModuleInit` (additive edit to the file US-003 created), the module registration test, unit and integration specs. Out: dispatch (US-003) and cancel (US-005); descriptors (US-001); `fleetWriteRefusal` (US-002). Also out: requeueing THREAD jobs, restricting to RUN/PLAN.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function requeueJobTool(
  fleetJobs: FleetJobsService,
  knowledge: KnowledgeIndexService,
): AssistantTool // parse -> { jobId }
```
acceptanceCriteria: requeueJobTool(...).parse({}) throws ToolInputError with reason 'jobId'

requeueJobTool(...).preview in project 'web' for a FAILED RUN job 'j1' with feature 'add-auth', ref 'trunk' and maxCostUsd '0.5', when resolveProjectRepo answers acme/app, returns exactly 'Requeue job j1 in web:\nRUN add-auth on acme/app @ trunk, now FAILED\nmax cost: $0.5'
requeueJobTool(...).preview for that job when resolveProjectRepo answers null and the job's repoId is 'r1' returns text whose second line is 'RUN add-auth on r1 @ trunk, now FAILED'
requeueJobTool(...).preview for a job whose state is 'RUNNING' throws ToolInputError with reason 'state'
requeueJobTool(...).preview for a CRASHED job whose command is 'THREAD' throws ToolInputError with reason 'command'
requeueJobTool(...).preview with ctx.projectId 'p1' for { jobId: 'j1' } reads the job through FleetJobsService.get with ('p1', 'j1')

userStories.title: koda_cancel_job
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `cancelJobTool` and register it in `FleetWriteTools`, so a thread can propose cancelling one active job of the project, run as the requester on approval.

**Motivation** — Today a thread can read jobs but cannot stop one; the user must leave the thread for the fleet page.

**Approach** — 2b2-R4 `koda_cancel_job` needs the CASL ability `update` `FleetJob` (permission `{ kind: 'ability', action: 'update', subject: 'FleetJob' }`). Cancel calls the service with `canOperate: true`; the route's own-job path for a requester without that ability is not exposed. For human roles this changes nothing: only DEVELOPER and ADMIN hold `create` `FleetJob`, and both hold `update`. 2b2-R5 A THREAD job is never cancelled through a tool.

2b2-D3 Input: `jobId` required; string of 1 to 64 characters; a violation throws `ToolInputError('jobId')`.

2b2-D4 Preview format (masked with `maskSecrets`), the job line matching the one `requeue-job-tool.ts` (US-004) builds:
```text
Cancel job j1 in web:
RUN add-auth on acme/app @ trunk, now RUNNING
```
The job line names the repository as `owner/name` through `KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo(projectId, { repoId })`, or as the job's `repoId` when that answers null.

2b2-D5 Preview checks: the job is read through `FleetJobsService.get(ctx.projectId, jobId)`, so a job of another project answers `not_found`. A THREAD job throws `ToolInputError('command')` (`isThreadKind`); this check runs before the state check, so a THREAD job in any state answers `command`. Cancel refuses a state `isTerminal` (from `fleet/jobs/job-state.ts`) accepts, with `ToolInputError('state')`. CONFIG_EDIT and CONFIG_DRIFT jobs are not restricted; the preview names their command.

2b2-D6 Execution: `FleetJobsService.cancel(ctx.actor.id, ctx.projectId, jobId, true)`. Result: `cancelled <jobId> /<slug>/fleet/jobs/<jobId>` when the answered state (`FleetJobDto`) is `CANCELLED`, else `cancel requested for <jobId> (<state>) /<slug>/fleet/jobs/<jobId>` (the runner reports `CANCELLED` later). Use `jobPath` from `tools/tool-input.ts`. A refusal the service throws becomes `ToolActionError('cancel refused: <text>')` where `<text>` is `fleetWriteRefusal(error)` (US-002). When that answers null the error is rethrown.

Integration tests (`POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_cancel_job?leaseEpoch=<n>`, decide at `POST /api/projects/web/fleet/approvals/:approvalId/decide`) follow the route, decide and job-seeding fixtures of `assistant-requeue-job-tool.integration.spec.ts` (created by US-004): the test creates the QUEUED RUN job it acts on with `prisma.fleetJob.create` on `acme/app` and a feature no other test uses. Each propose-then-approve pair is one `it`; tests pass in any order (`.nax/rules/api-test-isolation.md`).

**Scope** — In: `cancel-job-tool.ts`, registering it in `FleetWriteTools.onModuleInit` (additive edit to the file US-003 created), the module registration test, unit and integration specs. Out: dispatch (US-003) and requeue (US-004); descriptors (US-001); `fleetWriteRefusal` (US-002). Also out: cancelling THREAD jobs, the own-job cancel path without `update` `FleetJob`.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function cancelJobTool(
  fleetJobs: FleetJobsService,
  knowledge: KnowledgeIndexService,
): AssistantTool // parse -> { jobId }
```

analysis:
Koda S5b-2b-2 adds three fleet write tools (koda_dispatch_job, koda_requeue_job, koda_cancel_job) to the assistant write-tool machinery built in 2a (fleet-s5b-koda-actions) and 2b-1 (fleet-s5b-koda-write-tools, PR #298). A write tool is an AssistantTool (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts) = descriptor + parse + preview + execute. The executor (assistant-tool.executor.ts, proposeWrite/executeAction) already maps a preview's ToolInputError to 'invalid_input: <reason>', NotFoundAppException to 'not_found', and an execute's ToolActionError to a FAILED action carrying its text; any other error becomes 'error: <tool> failed'. This feature only adds the tools and fleetWriteRefusal, which turns the fleet services' 409/400 AppExceptions (read via AppException.prefix/.args) into ToolActionError text.

Pattern to mirror: apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/update-ticket-tool.ts (tool) and ticket-write-tools.ts (provider registering in onModuleInit via AssistantToolRegistry). Descriptors live in apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/koda-tool-descriptors.ts (WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS, KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS, kodaToolDescriptorsFor); the new FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS is appended last (REPO/PROJECT 22 descriptors, WORKSPACE 23, KODA_TOOL_LIMITS.maxTools is 32; each description must stay <= 2000 chars after the WORKSPACE sentence is appended, else apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts rejects the whole list). Existing koda-tool-descriptors.spec.ts assertions pin counts 19/20 and offsets by WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS.length; US-001 must update them exactly as the spec's Modifies lists (counts to 22/23, at(-1) name to koda_cancel_job, 'AC-2' test asserts five write entries precede the three fleet-write entries, AC-3/AC-15/AC-22 slices offset by WRITE+FLEET_WRITE lengths, AC-22 full-list equality gains ...FLEET_WRITE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS last).

Services called read-only: FleetJobsService.dispatch/requeue/cancel/get (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts), normalizeDispatch (fleet/jobs/dispatch-input.ts, throws ValidationAppException({reason}, 'fleet.dispatchInput')), canTransition/isTerminal (fleet/jobs/job-state.ts), isThreadKind (fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts), KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo(projectId, selector) returning KnowledgeRepoRef {id, owner, name, defaultBranch}. AssistantModule already imports FleetJobsModule and KnowledgeModule, so only the providers list gains FleetWriteTools. jobPath is currently a private helper in tools/fleet-tools.ts and moves unchanged to an export of tools/tool-input.ts (fleet-tools.ts then imports it).

Rulings: 2b2-R1 dispatch passes NO threadId (the calling thread is never idle so threads.busy would always fire); R2 maxCostUsd required; R3 no acknowledgeOpenPr (open PR fails the action); R4 requeue/cancel need update FleetJob and cancel passes canOperate=true; R5 THREAD jobs are never requeued/cancelled (preview ToolInputError('command') before the state check); R6 no pinnedRunnerId/selectorLabels/approvalTimeoutSec/acknowledgeOpenPr inputs.

Risks: (1) the descriptors spec edits must be exact or existing tests break; (2) the three stories share FleetWriteTools and assistant.module.spec.ts so US-003/004/005 are strictly sequential; (3) refusal tests must use the real fleetWriteRefusal, not a stub; (4) previews must be masked with maskSecrets (secret-shaped planFrom/feature must not leak); (5) dispatch execute re-resolves the repo and throws NotFoundAppException before calling the service if it no longer resolves; (6) dto passed to dispatch contains repoId plus only the input fields present (no undefined keys); (7) integration tests need the compose test DB (bun run test:db:up), follow test/integration/fleet/assistant-update-ticket-tool.integration.spec.ts fixtures (seedFleetHttpWorld, dev DEVELOPER, seedThreadJobFor RUNNING REPO THREAD job, FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true), use unique features per test, and obey .nax/rules/api-test-isolation.md; the requeue approve test seeds the job with selectorLabels ['no-such-label'] so it stays QUEUED. No Prisma, API contract or openapi.json change; no web, runner or protocol change. Immutability and small files per user style rules.
outOfScope: Binding a dispatched job to the calling thread, or reporting its progress or outcome back into the thread (2b2-R1).
A default `maxCostUsd`, or a cost cap stricter than the dispatch DTO's bounds and the existing budget policies (2b2-R2).
An `acknowledgeOpenPr` input; a RUN on a ticket with an open PR fails the action (2b2-R3).
`pinnedRunnerId`, `selectorLabels` and `approvalTimeoutSec` inputs to `koda_dispatch_job` (2b2-R6).
Cancelling a job through a tool on the strength of having requested it, without `update` `FleetJob` (2b2-R4).
Requeueing or cancelling a THREAD job through a tool (2b2-R5).
Dispatching CONFIG_EDIT, CONFIG_DRIFT or THREAD jobs; `koda_dispatch_job` takes `RUN` or `PLAN` only.
Any web change: the thread card, the inbox panel and the system notes already render every write tool from its preview text.
Changes to the runner, the fleet protocol or `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.
Editing a proposed action's input before deciding it (umbrella §12).
Rate limiting dispatches beyond the 2a cap on pending actions per thread and the existing budget policies.
Validating `ticketRefs` at preview; an unknown or unlinkable ticket fails the approved action with `dispatch refused: invalid ticket <ref>`.
Richer `invalid_input` refusal text (koda #299).
Placement details (the assigned runner id or misfits) in the action result.
US-003 only: a requester without `create` `FleetJob` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a); this feature adds no AC for it.
US-003 only: an unknown `command` answers `invalid_input: command` from the parser; this feature adds no AC for it.
US-003 only: a `maxCostUsd` below 0.0001, above 10000 or with more than 4 decimal places answers `invalid_input: maxCostUsd` from the parser (2b2-D3); this feature adds no AC for those bounds.
US-003 only: a repository that stops resolving between proposal and approval fails the action with `not_found` (2b2-D6); this feature adds no AC for it.
Restricting `koda_requeue_job` and `koda_cancel_job` to RUN and PLAN jobs; CONFIG_EDIT and CONFIG_DRIFT jobs are requeued and cancelled as the routes allow, and the preview names their command.
US-004 only: a requester without `update` `FleetJob` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a); this feature adds no AC for it.
US-005 only: a requester without `update` `FleetJob` (a VIEWER) is refused by the existing executor ability path (2a); this feature adds no AC for it.

US-004 only: a `jobId` of another project answers `not_found` through `FleetJobsService.get` and the existing executor preview mapping; this feature adds no `koda_requeue_job` AC for the not-found answer itself.
US-005 only: a `jobId` of another project answers `not_found` through `FleetJobsService.get` and the existing executor preview mapping; this feature adds no `koda_cancel_job` AC for it.
US-005 only: when the job's repository no longer resolves, the second preview line names the repository id instead of owner/name; this feature adds no `koda_cancel_job` AC for it.
A job whose state moves between the preview check and the approval is refused by the service at approval; the window is not locked at proposal.
